skill.name: tdd

content.value_statement: Test-first work often becomes brittle when teams test internals or write too many tests upfront. This skill guides Codex, Claude, and Claude Code through behavior-focused red-green-refactor cycles.
actual_capabilities: Plans TDD work around public interfaces and user-visible behaviors.
Guides one failing test, minimal implementation, and repeat cycles.
Explains when to mock external APIs, databases, time, randomness, and file systems.
Shows how to design interfaces that accept dependencies and avoid hidden side effects.
Provides refactoring checks after tests pass.
limitations: Does not provide a test runner or execute tests by itself.
Does not choose every edge case without user prioritization.
Focuses on behavior testing, not snapshot-heavy or implementation-detail tests.
Requires the agent to understand the project framework and existing test tools.

use_cases.title: Build a Feature Test First
use_cases.description: Use the skill to define one public behavior, write a failing test, implement the minimum code, and repeat.

use_cases.title: Repair Brittle Tests
use_cases.description: Use the guidance to replace internal mocks and private method assertions with behavior-focused tests through public interfaces.

use_cases.title: Review Testability Before Coding
use_cases.description: Use the interface design checklist to reduce side effects, inject dependencies, and create simpler boundaries for reliable tests.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a small feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd skill. Help me plan the public interface and the first behavior to test before writing implementation code.

prompt_templates.title: Write One Failing Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd skill. Write one behavior-focused failing test for this requirement, using the existing test framework and public APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor After Green
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd skill. The tests are green. Identify safe refactoring candidates and apply one small refactor at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign Brittle Test Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tdd skill. Audit these brittle tests, identify implementation coupling, and propose behavior-focused replacements with better boundaries.

output_examples.input: My tests break whenever I rename internal services.
output: A diagnosis of implementation-detail assertions and internal mocks.
Replacement test descriptions that verify observable behavior.
Boundary recommendations for mocks only around external systems.

output_examples.input: Review this module before I write tests.
output: Interface design feedback focused on dependency injection and return values.
Suggested behaviors to prioritize for the first TDD cycles.
Risks that should remain outside the initial test scope.

best_practices: Confirm the public interface and highest-value behaviors before writing tests.
Write one failing test, implement only enough code to pass, then repeat.
Mock only true system boundaries and keep tests focused on observable behavior.
anti_patterns: Writing every planned test before implementing the first behavior.
Mocking internal collaborators or asserting private implementation details.
Refactoring while tests are still failing.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents use test-driven development with small red-green-refactor cycles and behavior-focused tests.

faq.question: Does the skill execute tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance. The agent still uses the project test runner when appropriate.

faq.question: What kind of tests does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers integration-style tests through public interfaces that describe what the system does.

faq.question: When should I mock dependencies?
faq.answer: Mock external boundaries such as payment APIs, email services, time, randomness, and sometimes databases or file systems.

faq.question: Can it help refactor existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends refactoring only after tests pass and focuses on duplication, module depth, and natural design improvements.

faq.question: Is it useful for bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with a failing test that reproduces the bug through the public interface, then make the smallest fix.
